diagnostic_evidence.quote: In particular, if $\lambda=\Delta t^{-\frac{1}{2}}$, we obtain the minimal error rate

issues.failure_explanation: The paper's own mean-square bound is $(\max_i\mathbb{E}|Y_{t_i}-\mathcal{Y}_{t_i}|^2)^{1/2}\le C_2(\lambda\Delta t^{1/2}+\lambda^{-1})$ (Corollary cor:added-1). Substituting the advertised choice $\lambda=\Delta t^{-1/2}$ gives $\lambda\Delta t^{1/2}=1$ and $\lambda^{-1}=\Delta t^{1/2}$, i.e. a vacuous $O(1)$ bound, not $O(\Delta t^{1/4})$. Balancing the two terms requires $\lambda\Delta t^{1/2}\asymp\lambda^{-1}$, i.e. $\lambda\asymp\Delta t^{-1/4}$, at which both terms equal $\Delta t^{1/4}$. The stated tuning rule is therefore wrong by a square root, in both Introduction bullet 3 and the text following Corollary cor:added-1.

failure_location.quote:
under the natural terminal approximation, so that the balancing choice
$\lambda\asymp \Delta t^{-1/2}$ yields the rate $O(\Delta t^{1/4})$ for the value process.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\lambda\asymp\Delta t^{-1/2}$ by $\lambda\asymp\Delta t^{-1/4}$ in the two affected passages (Introduction bullet 3 and the sentence after Corollary cor:added-1); the displayed bound then yields the advertised $O(\Delta t^{1/4})$ rate directly. No other modification is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised parameter-coupling rule for the general Lipschitz (Z-dependent) case is false as stated: a reader choosing $\lambda=\Delta t^{-1/2}$ obtains only an $O(1)$ guarantee. The rate $O(\Delta t^{1/4})$ itself is correct (at $\lambda=\Delta t^{-1/4}$), and no labelled formal result is invalidated: Corollary cor:added-1's bound is correct, and the Z-independent tuning $\lambda\asymp\Delta t^{-1/2}$ used in Corollary cor:final and in the numerical experiments is correct.
issues.title: Wrong balancing rule for the O(Delta t^{1/4}) rate in the Z-dependent case
issues.why_classification: The repair is a single exponent correction to a stated tuning rule; the method, the advertised $O(\Delta t^{1/4})$ rate, and every downstream result (including the correctly stated Z-independent case and the experiments) survive unchanged, with no new argument required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
There exists a constant $\kappa>0$ such that, for all $(t,x)\in[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d$ and all $\xi\in\mathbb{R}^d$,
        \[
        \xi^\top \big(\sigma(t,x)\\sigma(t,x)^\top\big)\\,\xi \;\ge\; \kappa\,|\xi|^2.
        \]

issues.failure_explanation: The example's diffusion matrix $\sigma(s,x)=\sigma\,\mathrm{diag}(x^1,\dots,x^d)$ gives $\xi^\top\sigma\sigma^\top\xi=\sigma^2\sum_i (x^i)^2(\xi^i)^2$, which vanishes at $x=0$ for every $\xi$. Hence no $\kappa>0$ satisfies the ellipticity inequality on all of $[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d$: Assumption assumptions(ii) and Assumption assumptionpde(i) fail at the origin. The claim that these assumptions hold is therefore false as stated, and the same Black-Scholes dynamics underlie the Section 5 game-put experiment, which is thus formally outside the hypotheses of the paper's theorems.

failure_location.quote: Then, it is straightforward to check that Assumptions~\ref{assumptions} and~\ref{assumptionpde} hold.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reformulate the example and the experiment in log-price coordinates ($\tilde X^i=\log X^i$, giving a constant, uniformly elliptic diffusion $\sigma$) and re-verify Assumptions assumption2 for the transformed barriers, which remain piecewise $C^{1,2}$ with kinks on the log-transformed hypersurfaces; alternatively, localize the theory to a truncated state space bounded away from the degenerate point. Either restores formal applicability without changing any rate or conclusion.
issues.overall_effect: The motivating Israeli-option example, and with it the theoretical justification of the Section 5 numerical experiment, does not satisfy the global uniform-ellipticity hypotheses; formally, none of the results assuming Assumptions assumptions and assumptionpde applies to the Black-Scholes model as written. No theorem statement is false and no rate or complexity guarantee is lost.
issues.title: Black-Scholes example violates the global uniform ellipticity hypotheses
issues.why_classification: The failure is confined to an illustrative example's false claim that the global assumptions hold; the standard log-coordinate repair is contained, restores all hypotheses, and changes no theorem, rate, or advertised scope, since every formal result explicitly carries the ellipticity hypotheses.

issues.failure_explanation: Run backward from the terminal condition, each step requires solving the implicit scalar equation $\mathcal{Y}^{\lambda,\pi}_{t_i}=\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{Y}^{\lambda,\pi}_{t_{i+1}}|\mathcal{F}_{t_i}]+f_\lambda(t_i,X^{\tilde\pi}_{t_i},\mathcal{Y}^{\lambda,\pi}_{t_i},\mathcal{Z}^{\lambda,\pi}_{t_i})\Delta t$. Since $\partial_y f_\lambda\le K_y$ (the penalty terms only decrease the slope outside the corridor $[p_b,p_w]$), the map $y\mapsto y-f_\lambda(t_i,x,y,z)\\Delta t$ has slopes $\ge 1-K_y\Delta t$; it is strictly monotone and coercive, hence uniquely solvable, only when $\Delta t\,K_y<1$. The stated hypotheses ($\lambda>2K_y$, $\Delta t<1/(16K_z^2)$) do not imply this (e.g. large $K_y$, small $K_z$), so under them the implicit equation may have no solution or several, and the error bounds are quantified over an object that may fail to exist or be ambiguous.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the well-posedness condition $\Delta t\,K_y<1$ to the hypotheses of the scheme and of the theorems quantifying over it (or state them for $\Delta t$ small enough to satisfy both $\Delta t K_y<1$ and $\Delta t<1/(16K_z^2)$). Under the advertised tunings ($\lambda\asymp\Delta t^{-1/2}$ or $\Delta t^{-1/4}$ with $\Delta t\to0$) this is automatic, so all bounds and rates are preserved.
issues.overall_effect: Under the stated parameter regime the backward recursion defining the scheme may fail to be uniquely solvable, so the discretization error bounds (Theorems discerror and better) and the total-error corollaries (cor:added-1, cor:final), which quantify over triples satisfying the scheme, are asserted without the scheme being guaranteed to exist. The advertised rates are unaffected once the missing smallness condition is added, since it holds automatically under the paper's tuning rules.
issues.title: Implicit backward scheme is not well-posed under the stated hypotheses
issues.why_classification: The defect is a single missing local smallness condition; adding it (or noting it is automatic for small $\Delta t$ under the tuning rules) restores well-posedness with no change to any bound, rate, or conclusion, and no new construction or argument is required.
